spec_documentation_note: Read on 2026-10-24. The SPEC kit (sources, obstacle files, expected output) was not available, so the upstream below is still the closest openly licensed copy of the SPEC lbm code (Thomas Pohl's D3Q19 lattice Boltzmann kernel, SPEC CPU2006 470.lbm / CPU2017 519.lbm_r lineage), not the SPEC source. See COMPATIBILITY.md for what the page settles and what still needs the kit.

spec_documentation_facts.author: Thomas Pohl, licensed to SPEC directly by the author; no Parboil mention
spec_documentation_facts.command_line: lbm <time steps> <result file> <0: nil, 1: cmp, 2: str> <0: ldc, 1: channel flow> [<obstacle file>]
spec_documentation_facts.refrate: 1200 time steps on an obstacle file, 200 x 200 x 130 domain
spec_documentation_facts.test_train: same geometry as refrate, fewer time steps (counts not stated)
spec_documentation_facts.obstacle_format: ASCII; '.' is a fluid cell, any other character ('#') an obstacle cell
spec_documentation_facts.output: statistics summary on stdout; action 2 writes binary little-endian vx/vy/vz per cell, single precision by default (double selectable in config.h)
spec_documentation_facts.validation: SPEC validates the stdout statistics summary; the cmp action reports the maximum absolute per-cell velocity difference against a threshold
spec_documentation_facts.changes_vs_519: highly similar to 519.lbm_r, resized to about 1.6 GiB (about 4x CPU2017); SPEC_LBM_NO_HUGE_ARRAY for systems that cannot allocate large static arrays
spec_documentation_facts.not_stated: internal precision (1.6 GiB = 200*200*130 cells * 20 entries * 2 grids * 8 bytes implies double), lattice (D3Q19), test/train step counts, which simulation type refrate uses

license: University of Illinois/NCSA Open Source License (upstream/lbm/LICENSE)
status: Unmodified Parboil CPU version of the SPEC lbm kernel; not the SPEC distribution. Validation uses the documented double-precision adaptation in benchmarks/lbm/reference/.
vine_pin: evaluations/vine-pin.json (unchanged; no Vine changes were needed)
